source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
Prime DFW01-01 publishes 20 MW of IT capacity across 213,000 square feet of technical space in Dallas. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 20 MW supports roughly 500 racks; at 10 kW per rack, a common colocation density, the same load supports roughly 2,000 racks. The operator has not published a target rack density, so which figure applies is unknown. The 213,000 square feet works out to approximately 94 watts per square foot at the published IT load, which sits toward the lower end of AI-optimized facilities and suggests the space may be sized for mixed or general-purpose colocation rather than dense GPU clusters, though that inference depends on layout assumptions the operator has not published.

SOC 2 Type 2 certification means the facility has passed an independent audit of its security controls over a defined period, qualifying it to host regulated enterprise workloads. ISO 27001 certification means it has implemented and had audited an information security management system, qualifying it for customers with that contractual requirement. Neither certification speaks to power redundancy tier or cooling capacity.

Within Texas, this site ranks sixth among the thirteen facilities on this site that have published a megawatt figure, out of 133 total mapped facilities in the state. Those thirteen facilities account for 389 MW of published IT capacity in aggregate, and DFW01-01's 20 MW represents roughly 5 percent of that published total. The remaining 120 mapped Texas facilities have published no capacity figure, so the 389 MW figure understates true state capacity by an unknown amount, and the sixth-place rank reflects only what operators have chosen to disclose.
